_comment: The syllabus outline used to sequence the exam-prep question bank.
The unit content and session counts are taken from the official SRMIST
syllabus supplied by the learner: 'Academic Curricula, Regulations
2026, Volume 2 - Syllabi for First Year Courses', the Programming for
Problem Solving entry on printed page 62.
The official syllabus names the units only as 'Unit 1' to 'Unit 5' and
gives no titles, so the titles here are descriptive labels derived from
the official session content. Each is marked as such in the record.
The 'keywords' list is the mechanism for placing a question in a
syllabus unit. It is a *matching aid*, not a claim about the question:
the app records which keywords matched, and the question's own paper
unit is never overwritten. A question whose keywords match more than one
unit equally is left unassigned rather than being forced into one.
source: Official SRMIST syllabus, Regulations 2026 Volume 2, course entry on printed page 62 (PDF page 62).

units.title: Fundamentals of C: types, expressions and decision-making
units.official_content: Simple data types (int, float, char) in C and their size, range and applications; assignment and arithmetic expressions; operator precedence; decision-making with if...else if...else; Boolean and relational expressions; switch statements and menu-driven programs; user-defined input and output.

units.title: Problem decomposition, functions and modular design
units.official_content: Decomposing a problem into sub-tasks and choosing a function type for each; pass-by-value and pass-by-reference functions; pointer concepts for accessing and manipulating memory; helper functions and modularisation; functions with and without return values; recursive thinking, call stack, recurrence relations; factorial, Fibonacci, digit counting, GCD and palindrome by recursion.

units.title: Arrays, strings, pointers and recursion
units.official_content: Arrays and strings: declaring, initialising and indexing 1-D arrays and strings; contiguous memory layout; inbuilt string functions strlen, strcmp, strrev, strcpy, strcat, strchr, strstr; pointers into arrays and strings; bubble sort with iteration tracing; 2-D arrays and matrices; while, do-while and for loops; binary and linear search; frequency counting; recursion over arrays and strings.

units.title: Nested loops, sorting, searching and memory use
units.official_content: Nested loops: tracing execution, counting iterations, generating and printing patterns, traversing 2-D arrays; bubble sort with iteration tracing; hollow squares; sparse matrices; searching an array for a record; binary and linear search; comparing recursion with iteration on stack usage and call overhead; break and continue inside iterative structures; reading a file of numbers and producing a frequency count; reading a file line by line and counting characters, words and lines.

units.title: Structures, dynamic memory and file handling
units.official_content: Structures: grouping heterogeneous data under one name, arrays of structures, functions taking structures by value and by reference, functions returning an updated structure; dynamic memory: malloc, calloc, realloc and free, resizing arrays, dynamic lists; file handling: fopen, fscanf, fgets, feof and fclose, reading text files into variables and arrays, counting, summation and averaging; modular programming with structures.

_previous_units_note: The past papers and question banks the learner supplied are from the earlier regulation and carry the unit names above. The 2026 syllabus reorganises the course, so a paper's unit number does not map one-to-one onto a 2026 unit. The paper's own unit is the authoritative attribution and is what the question bank is sequenced by; the 2026 unit is shown as a cross-reference only, and only where the match is confident.
